# Side questions, public skills and founder setup

Use `/btw <question>` to ask a temporary side question while the main conversation continues. The answer appears above the editor. `/btw cancel` stops that question, `/btw clear` hides it, and `/btw show` restores the latest result. Side questions do not enter conversation history or run tools.

## Install the maintained setup

```sh
pitty founders-setup --dry-run
pitty founders-setup
pitty founders-setup --check
```

The setup installs the maintained plugins, 17 curated skills and 11 agent profiles. Agent profiles leave model and thinking settings unset. Existing model defaults, credentials, unrelated packages and custom agent files remain in place. DoppelClaude stays inactive until its provider is configured, so a fresh installation can start with other providers.

[PiTTy-Skills](https://github.com/mistrjirka/PiTTy-Skills) and [PiTTy-BTW](https://github.com/mistrjirka/PiTTy-BTW) are public MIT-licensed repositories. Anyone can install, edit or fork them. `--skills-source` and `--btw-source` select a fork or local checkout. Later setup runs remember that choice.

The first-install scripts accept `--founders-setup` or `-FoundersSetup`. Founder setup requires Node.js 24 or newer on Linux, macOS or WSL. It prepares the supported managed Pi runtime without replacing global Pi.

## Extension widgets

PiTTy now displays string widgets from any extension above or below the editor. Widgets preserve ANSI styles, wrap in narrow terminals, and scroll within a bounded area. Updates preserve the editor draft and focus, including while dialogs are open. Widgets remain separate from saved conversation messages.

## Provider and conversation compatibility

Supported API providers reuse a safe main-request prefix and cache identity for a tool-free side request. Cache savings depend on the provider and are not guaranteed. DoppelClaude uses its existing Claude query's separate side-question request. It requires a live main query plus the user's provider configuration and Claude sign-in.

An unsupported provider or unsafe context produces an explicit error. Existing conversations require no migration. Restart PiTTy after installation to load the updated managed runtime.
